data.short_meaning: God of the Sun and Light
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Apollo is the god of the Sun, music, poetry, art, and prophecy. He is also associated with archery, plague, medicine, and knowledge. The name Apollo carries the meaning “God of the Sun and Light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Apollo usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the sun and light and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Apollo belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the Sun and Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Apollo total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Apollo was one of the most significant and widely recognized deities in the Greek pantheon. He was often depicted with the lyre, a stringed musical instrument, and was considered a god of arts, creativity, and culture. The term "apollo" is now used in the Western world as a synonym for "sun god" - a symbol of light, warmth, and life-giving energy.
data.spiritual_significance: For ancient Greeks, Apollo was a god of music and poetry because he was believed to inspire these artistic pursuits. He was also considered a protector and healer, especially in the areas of medicine and prophecy. To follow the spirit of Apollo is to engage in creative and artistic pursuits, to seek knowledge and wisdom, and to feel the warmth and light of the sun in our lives.
